questions.stem: Which food helps your body grow?
questions.explanation: An egg is a body-building food. It helps you grow. Fish, dal and milk help you grow too.

questions.stem: Which foods should we eat often? Which only a little?
questions.explanation: Rice, eggs and green vegetables give us energy, help us grow and keep us healthy. Sweets, chips and doughnuts are fine only as a small treat.

questions.stem: A balanced diet has some of each kind of food and plenty of ___.
questions.explanation: We need to drink plenty of water every day, as well as eating different kinds of food.

questions.stem: Washing your hands with soap gets rid of germs.
questions.explanation: Soap and water wash germs off your hands. Clean hands help stop you getting ill.

questions.stem: A fizzy drink is the best drink for a healthy body.
questions.explanation: Water is the best drink for your body. Fizzy drinks are full of sugar and do not help you grow.

questions.stem: How can you keep your body healthy? Choose all that are right.
questions.explanation: Exercise, clean hands and clean teeth keep us healthy. We also need plenty of sleep and many kinds of food, not only sweets.

questions.stem: Match each picture to what it does for your body.
questions.explanation: Rice and roti give us energy. Fish, egg and dal help us grow. Fruit and vegetables protect us. We also drink plenty of water.

questions.stem: Children need to sleep about ___ hours every night.
questions.explanation: Children need about 10 hours of sleep. Sleep rests the body and helps us feel good the next day.

questions.stem: Put the steps for washing hands in order.
questions.explanation: Wet your hands first, then use soap and rub for 20 seconds. Rinse the soap away and dry your hands last.

questions.stem: Which meal is the most balanced?
options: chips, a sweet cake and a fizzy drink
questions.explanation: Rice gives energy, fish helps us grow, spinach keeps us healthy, and water is the best drink. The other meals have no body-building or protecting foods.

questions.stem: Rice and roti give us ___.
questions.explanation: Rice, roti and potato are energy foods. They give us the energy to play and learn.

questions.stem: Class 1 put pretend germs (glitter) on their hands, then washed. Spots left: water 5 seconds, 30. Water 20 seconds, 15. Soap 20 seconds, 2. Which way cleaned best?
questions.explanation: Fewer spots mean cleaner hands. Soap for 20 seconds left only 2 spots, so it cleaned best.

questions.stem: Which food helps protect your body and keeps you healthy?
questions.explanation: Green vegetables and fruit have vitamins and fibre. They protect us and keep us healthy.

questions.stem: Which pictures show healthy habits? Choose all that are right.
questions.explanation: Washing with soap, running and brushing your teeth keep you healthy. Sweets and doughnuts are only for a small treat.

questions.stem: Match each picture to why it helps.
questions.explanation: Soap removes germs, brushing cleans teeth, sleep rests the body and running makes muscles strong.

questions.stem: Rafi's lunch is chips, a sweet cake and a fizzy drink. What should he change?
options: Drink water and add a banana.
questions.explanation: Water is a better drink, and a banana is a protecting food. Rafi also needs foods that help him grow, such as rice, dal or fish.

questions.stem: Tumpa watched cartoons until late. At school she is sleepy. What should she do tonight?
questions.explanation: Her body needs sleep. Going to bed early helps her feel awake and ready to play at school.

questions.stem: Mina has been playing football in the mud. Now it is time to eat lunch. What should she do first?
options: Wipe her hands on her shirt.
Wash her hands with soap and water.
questions.explanation: Muddy hands can carry germs. Washing with soap and water before eating helps keep us well.

questions.stem: Anika feels grumpy after a long day. Resting or playing with friends can help her feel better.
questions.explanation: Rest and fun help our bodies and our feelings. Playing with friends and relaxing keep us happy and well.

questions.stem: Anika wants to be active every day. What can she do? Choose all that are right.
questions.explanation: Walking, playing cricket and skipping make our bodies move and grow strong. Sitting or lying down all day does not.

questions.stem: Tumpa feels tired at school. Give her one tip to feel better.
questions.model_answer: Go to bed early, or eat a good breakfast, or play outside.
questions.explanation: A tired body needs sleep, good food and exercise. Any of these tips can help Tumpa feel better.

questions.stem: Nadia's dinner is rice, roti and potato. What should she add to make it balanced?
questions.explanation: Rice, roti and potato are all energy foods. Fish helps her grow and spinach protects her, so she needs both.

questions.stem: In the glitter test, water for 5 seconds left 30 spots. Soap for 20 seconds left 2 spots. How many fewer spots did soap for 20 seconds leave?
questions.explanation: 30 take away 2 is 28. Soap for 20 seconds took away 28 more spots than water for 5 seconds.

questions.stem: Water for 5 seconds left 30 glitter spots. Soap for 20 seconds left 2 spots. Sumi says: 'They clean just as well.' Is Sumi right?
questions.explanation: 30 spots is much more than 2 spots. Soap and 20 seconds cleaned much better than a quick rinse.
